A taste of what you’ll do

The Regulatory Counsel is a mid-level role within the Regulatory function, responsible for providing independent regulatory advice and analysis to the business across multiple gambling jurisdictions.

The Regulatory Counsel takes ownership of a defined portfolio of regulatory matters, providing clear and practical advice on the application of gambling laws, licence conditions, and regulatory requirements.

The role involves independent management of licensing and regulatory submissions, proactive identification of regulatory risks, and substantive input into the development of policies, frameworks, and business initiatives. The Regulatory Counsel will develop relationships with internal stakeholders and regulators, contributing meaningfully to the delivery of the team’s objectives.

Accountabilities:

Regulatory Advisory & Interpretation

    Monitor, analyse and interpret regulatory developments across multiple gambling jurisdictions, assessing their impact on the business.
    Provide clear, practical, and independent regulatory advice to internal stakeholders across product, marketing, payments, operations, and technology.
    Conduct substantive legal research and regulatory analysis on applicable laws, licence conditions, and regulatory frameworks.
    Manage regulatory queries from the business, providing timely and well-reasoned responses with limited supervision.
    Provide regulatory input on customer-facing terms and conditions, complaints, and related matters.
    Identify and escalate novel, complex, or high-risk regulatory issues to the Senior Regulatory Counsel as appropriate.

Regulatory Strategy & Business Enablement

    Lead regulatory impact assessments in connection with new products, features, market entries, and strategic initiatives.
    Identify, assess, and advise on regulatory risks, contributing to risk assessments and mitigation strategies.
    Drive cross-functional engagement to support the embedding of regulatory requirements across the business.
    Provide substantive regulatory guidance on AML/CFT, sanctions, responsible gambling, data protection, and other key regulatory areas.
    Support the Senior Regulatory Counsel in providing regulatory input into the business’s strategic planning and commercial activities.

Licensing & Regulatory Operations

    Manage the preparation, submission, and ongoing maintenance of gaming licence applications across multiple jurisdictions, taking ownership of assigned portfolios.
    Oversee and ensure compliance with regulatory reporting obligations, including timely and accurate submissions to licensing authorities.
    Maintain and develop regulatory registers, licences, approvals, and associated documentation.
    Manage and develop relationships with regulators and competent authorities, escalating significant regulatory interactions to the Senior Regulatory Counsel.
    Prepare and coordinate responses to regulatory inquiries, inspections, enforcement actions, and information requests.

Regulatory Framework & Policy Development

    Assist in the development and maintenance of assigned regulatory policies, standards, and frameworks, ensuring alignment with applicable laws and licence conditions.
    Provide substantive regulatory input into AML, responsible gambling, consumer protection, and other regulatory policy areas.
    Develop and deliver regulatory training and awareness materials to Compliance and operational teams.
    Identify gaps in existing policies and frameworks and propose improvements proactively.

Governance, Assurance & Collaboration

    Provide meaningful regulatory input into compliance monitoring activities, internal reviews, and audit processes.
    Collaborate closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Technology, and operational teams to ensure consistent interpretation and application of regulatory requirements across the business.
    Lead or contribute to regulatory workstreams within internal projects, change program, and cross-functional initiatives.
    Support junior members of the Regulatory team, providing guidance and reviewing their work where required.

Documentation & General

    Maintain accurate and up-to-date regulatory documentation, records, and internal registers.
    Contribute to the continuous improvement of the Regulatory function’s processes and ways of working.
    Perform other duties reasonably aligned with the role.

Qualifications

    Qualified lawyer with a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Law (LLB or equivalent).

Required Skills

    3–4 years post-qualification experience in regulatory, legal, or advisory roles, ideally within iGaming, fintech, financial services, or other regulated industries.
    Demonstrated experience in multi-jurisdictional gambling regulation and licensing, including the preparation and management of licence applications and regulatory submissions.
    Experience providing independent regulatory advice to internal business stakeholders.
    Exposure to AML/CFT, responsible gambling, and consumer protection regulatory requirements is required.
    Strong legal research, analysis, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and address regulatory issues independently.
    Ability to interpret complex regulatory requirements and translate them into clear, practical, and commercially sound advice.
    Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present regulatory analysis to non-legal audiences.
    Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage a varied and demanding workload, prioritize effectively, and meet deadlines.
    High level of professionalism, integrity, and attention to detail.
    Fluency in English is required; proficiency in an additional language (Danish, Finnish, or Swedish) is advantageous.

Preferred Skills

jobs.title: Ajoneuvovarustelija
jobs.description:
**Hifix Oy hakee ajoneuvovarustelijaa osaksi kasvavaa tiimiämme!**

Etsimme käytännönläheistä ja oma-aloitteista ajoneuvovarustelijaa, joka nauttii käsillä tekemisestä ja haluaa työskennellä monipuolisten hyötyajoneuvojen varustelutehtävien parissa.

Työtehtäviin kuuluu erilaisten paketti- ja hyötyajoneuvojen varustelua asiakkaiden tarpeiden mukaan. Työ on vaihtelevaa ja sisältää sekä valmiiden tuotteiden asentamista että yksilöllisten ratkaisujen rakentamista.

**Työtehtäviisi kuuluu esimerkiksi:**

- hyötyajoneuvojen varustelu ja kalustaminen

- työkaluhyllyjen, laatikostojen ja muiden säilytysratkaisujen asennukset

- vanerointi ja ajoneuvojen sisätilojen rakentaminen

- kattotelineiden, astinlautojen ja muiden varusteiden asennukset

- lisävalojen ja muiden ajoneuvojen sähkövarusteiden asennukset

- erilaisten rakenteiden valmistus ja sovittaminen ajoneuvoihin

- asiakkaiden tilaamien yksilöllisten varusteluratkaisujen toteuttaminen

- tarvittaessa myös muut ajoneuvojen varusteluun ja asennukseen liittyvät työtehtävät


**Mitä odotamme sinulta?**

Toivomme sinulta ennen kaikkea hyvää tekemisen meininkiä, huolellisuutta ja oma-aloitteisuutta.

Arvostamme kykyä ratkaista käytännön ongelmia ja halua oppia uusia asioita.

Aikaisempi kokemus ajoneuvojen varustelusta on eduksi, mutta tehtävään voidaan kouluttaa sopiva tekijä, jolla on vahva käytännön osaaminen ja kiinnostus alaan.

**Eduksi katsomme erityisesti**

- kokemuksen hyötyajoneuvojen varustelusta

- puuntyöstötaidot ja kokemuksen vaneritöistä

- laiterakennus- ja metallityötaidot

- ajoneuvosähköjen tuntemuksen

- kokemuksen sähköasennuksista ja 12 V järjestelmistä

- teknisen piirustuksen lukutaidon

- hyvän työkalujen ja koneiden tuntemuksen


**Millainen henkilö sopii meille?**

Olet käytännönläheinen tekijä, joka haluaa nähdä oman työnsä lopputuloksen. Osaat käyttää erilaisia käsityökaluja ja koneita, etkä säikähdä uusia tai haastavia asennustehtäviä.

Meillä arvostetaan erityisesti sitä, että työntekijä pystyy miettimään itse ratkaisuja ja viemään työn alusta loppuun huolellisesti.

**Mitä tarjoamme?**

Hifix Oy:llä pääset tekemään monipuolista ja vaihtelevaa työtä hyötyajoneuvojen varustelun parissa. Työkohteet vaihtelevat ja työssä pääsee toteuttamaan sekä valmiita varustelukokonaisuuksia että asiakkaiden yksilöllisiä ratkaisuja.

Tarjoamme mahdollisuuden kehittää omaa osaamista monipuolisesti autojen, rakentamisen, sähköjen ja teknisten ratkaisujen parissa.

**Työsuhde**: vakituinen

**Työpaikka:** Lahti

**Aloitus**: sopimuksen mukaan

**Palkkaus**: sopimuksen mukaan / kokemuksen ja osaamisen perusteella

**Kiinnostuitko?**

Lähetä hakemuksesi ja kerro lyhyesti itsestäsi, aikaisemmasta työkokemuksestasi sekä siitä, millaista käytännön osaamista sinulla on.

**Hakemukset: info@hifix.fi**

jobs.title: Ph.D.-scholarship in numerical optimisation of wind assisted propulsion systems
jobs.description:
Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, has a vacancy for PhD Research Fellow in numerical optimisation of wind assisted propulsion systems

Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (Høgskulen på Vestlandet, HVL) has an open Ph.D. position with a project period of 4 years at the Department of Mechanical Engineering and Maritime Studies. The Ph.D. candidate will be part of an interdisciplinary project involving three research groups on energy and environmental technology, on wind, water and waves and on data science. 

Due to the nature of the work to be carried out in the project, the candidate will be a part of the Ph.D.-programme Computer Science: Software Engineering, Sensor Networks and Engineering Computing. (https://www.hvl.no/en/research/phd-programmes/phd-programme-in-computer-science/). The research programme in Computer Science currently includes 20 professors and associate professors, more than 30 PhD and post-doctoral fellows, and a large number of master’s students.

This programme is located at the Faculty of Technology, Environmental and Social Sciences at Western Norway University of Applied Sciences. PhD research fellows receive an annual work expense funding which can be used for conference participation, research visits, and equipment.

Workplace will be at HVL Campus Bergen.


Tasks and areas of responsibility:

Wind Assisted Propulsion Systems (WAPS) are moving from demonstration to commercial scale. Rotor sails and rigid wing sails are currently installed on tankers, bulkers, and Ro-Ro vessels, and a growing number of wind-cargo ships are being purpose-built for sail propulsion. Sails reduce the ship’s onboard energy demand, and with it fuel consumption and emissions.


This PhD project will develop simulation and optimisation methods for modern sail design based on the Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) and Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) as part of the optimisation loop. The developed method will be applied to optimise both existing sail technologies and novel concepts depending on ship size, route, and operation in order to determine fuel and emission savings.
 

The project will extend an existing Julia LBM in-house code, with established HPC LBM frameworks as references, benchmarks, and potential building blocks combined with Bayesian optimisation.

As part of the required duties (25% of the position), the candidate will join the team focusing on regional development at the faculty and the department. This might include:


• Promote more externally funded research projects in collaboration between our research environment and the shipping industry.
• Interact with regional, national and international partners, and work to promote cooperation between the department and the surrounding society (e.g., bachelor and master theses).
• Mobilization to promote research-based innovation in the shipping industry in collaboration with our participation in the project FORREGION Vestland.
• Supporting the department in our work related to lifelong learning in the shipping industry, with emphasis on strengthening the portfolio of flexible and decentralized education.


Qualifications (requirements):

•Admission to the PhD programme requires that the applicant holds a master’s degree in computer science or a closely related field, such as a master’s degree in informatics, software engineering, communication systems, engineering computing, scientific computing, or computational engineering.
•Candidates from other natural sciences or engineering disciplines holding a master’s degree with a strong emphasis on ICT and computing, for example mechanical, marine or aerospace engineering, applied mathematics or computational physics, may also qualify for admission to the PhD programme.
•Admission into the programme requires that the applicant has obtained strong grades for both the master’s thesis and the course work of the master’s degree. Specifically, admission into the programme normally requires that the applicant has obtained:
- a grade of B (Norwegian/ECTS scale) or better on the master’s thesis,
- an average grade higher than C (Norwegian/ECTS scale) on the coursework associated with the master’s degree
•Documented programming skills beyond scripting in Julia, or in a language Julia can call (Python, C, C++, Fortran).

The PhD research fellow must enrol in the PhD programme in Computer Science: Software Engineering, Sensor Networks and Engineering Computing at Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, and must meet the formal admission requirements for admission into the PhD programme. The position is announced for a period of 4 years with 25% of the 4-year period will be designated to duties such as teaching, development and administrative tasks.

The PhD candidate will be assigned two academic supervisors at Western Norway University of Applied Sciences. An application for enrolment should first be submitted after an appointment is made and the supervisors will help with this procedure. The candidate must be enrolled as a PhD student within 3 months from the start of the employment.


Favoured qualifications (not requirements):

- Master’s thesis in computational fluid dynamics, ideally applied to wings, foils, rotors, or similar configurations.
- Knowledge of and experience with Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM), Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) and/or Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)
- Knowledge of and experience with optimisation methods.

 

Personal abilities:

- Ability to contribute towards a good work environment and in teamwork.
- Excellent communication skills, ability to communicate well in both written and spoken English. Proficiency, written and spoken, in a Scandinavian language is an advantage.
- The candidate must be diligent and display the ability to work independently, supplemented with regular guidance, and is expected to carry out high-quality research and to publish the results in international workshops, conferences, and journals.

 

Candidates who have submitted a master’s thesis and who have not yet been awarded a master’s degree may also qualify for the position, provided that the master`s degree is awarded within four weeks of the deadline for applications to this position. Proof of successfully finishing the master’s degree along with the grade for the thesis and the final average grade must be submitted to HVL as soon as possible. Applicants already holding a Ph.D. are not eligible for this position.


In addition to the required educational and scientific background, the following criteria will be evaluated: competence and grades on completed course work, quality of the master's thesis, publications (if any), research and teaching experience, practical software engineering skills and experience. A possible outline of a research plan for a potential PhD project will also be taken into account.

The PhD candidate will be assigned two academic supervisor(s) at Western Norway University of Applied Sciences. The necessary application to join the Ph.D. programme Computer Science: Software Engineering, Sensor Networks and Engineering Computing must be submitted and accepted within 3 months of starting in the position. The supervisors will help with this procedure.


Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is subjected to the regulation for export control system. The regulation might be applied in the processing of the applications.


For more information, contact: Associate Prof. Norbert Lümmen: Norbert.Lummen@hvl.no 


Application procedure:

Applications will be evaluated by an expert panel of three members.

Applicants are asked to submit their application and CV online. Please use the link “Apply for this job” (“Søk stillingen”).

The following documentation must be uploaded as an attachment to the online application:


•A brief cover letter including a description of research interests and motivation for working within the current project. The cover letter should include a detailed justification of your qualifications in relation to the listed requirements.
•CV (summarizing education, positions and a complete list of academic publications)
•Master thesis
•Transcripts and diplomas of bachelor’s and master’s degrees. If you have not yet completed your master’s degree, please submit a statement from your institution confirming the expected date of award of your master’s degree.
•Diplomas and certificatesAt least one letter of recommendation preferably from a previous academic supervisor.
•Names and contact details of 2 references. One of these should be the main supervisor of the master’s thesis.

At least one letter of recommendation preferably from a previous academic supervisor.

In case the applicant already has publications, a complete list of these and copies of up to five selected publications should be uploaded. Applicants should indicate which of these publications or parts of these publications should be given special consideration in the evaluation.

If the documents submitted are not in a Scandinavian language or in English, the applicants must submit certified translations of these. The transcripts must specify the topics, the course works, and the grades at the bachelor`s and master`s degree levels. It is required that the applicant encloses a recognition document showing that their degree is equivalent to a Norwegian bachelor’s degree, master’s degree, or PhD. You can read more about applying for recognition of foreign higher education here.

The Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir) offers an automatic recognition document for certain degrees from selected countries. If the applicant’s degree is covered by the automatic recognition, it will be sufficient to attach this document. Read more about automatic recognition here.

As the HK-dir application process may take some time it is recommended to apply to HK-dir as soon as possible. If you have not received a recognition document from HK- dir within the  application deadline, please enclose documentation from HK-dir showing that they have received your application.

Applicants should note that the evaluation will be based on the documentation submitted electronically via Jobbnorge within the submission deadline. The applicants are responsible for ensuring that all the documentation is submitted before the closing date. It is of utmost importance that all publications to be considered in the evaluation are uploaded as an attachment with the application, since these are sent electronically to the expert panel. Applications cannot be sent by e-mail or to individuals at HVL.

Applicants may be called in for an interview.


Salary:
  • Good occupational pension, insurance and loan schemes from The Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
  • Exciting academic environment with the possibility of competence enhancement and development
  • Opportunities for training within the working hours 

The Research Fellow position is compensated according to position code 1017 Research Fellow.

There is a compulsory 2 % deduction to the pension fund (see http://www.spk.no for more information). The successful applicant must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.


General information:

The appointment will be made in accordance with the regulations for State employees Law in Norway ("Lov om statens ansatte)". Organizational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities associated with the position must be expected.

State employment shall reflect the multiplicity of the population at large to the highest possible degree. Western Norway University of Applied Sciences Bergen has therefore adopted a personnel policy objective to ensure that we achieve a balanced age and gender composition and the recruitment of persons of various ethnic backgrounds.

Information about the applicant may be made public even though the applicant has requested not to be named in the list of applicants. The applicant will be notified if his/her request is not respected.

Short-listed applicants will be called in for an interview.

Employed on condition that you are granted a work and residence permit (must be considered individually).

Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is subjected to The Export Control Regulation. The regulation will be applied in the processing of the applications.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Høgskulen på Vestlandet (HVL) er en av de største høgskolene i landet, med om lag 1 800 tilsette og 16 000 studenter fordelt på fem campus i Førde, Sogndal, Bergen, Stord og Haugesund. Hvert år uteksaminerer vi 3000 kandidater som er med på å løse viktige samfunnsoppgaver.


HVL har sterke og innovative fagmiljø innen helse- og sosialvitskap, ingeniør- og maritime utdanningar, lærer-, kultur- og idrettsfag, natur- og samfunnsvitskap, og økonomi og ledelse. HVL skal være tett på arbeidslivet, regionen og studentene. Den overordnet ambisjonen vår er å bli et universitet med en tydelig profesjons- og arbeidslivsrettet profil.


HVL sin visjon er "Kunnskap som bygger menneske og samfunn". Strategiske ambisjoner og mål har særlig oppmerksom på berekraftig samfunnsutvikling, velferd og innovasjon, forankret i våre verdier - inkludere, utfordre og samhandle - som kjennetegner identiteten og kulturen hos oss.


 Fakultetet for teknologi, miljø- og samfunnsvitskap har et bredt utdanningstilbud både på bachelor og masternivå innenfor ingeniør- og naturfag, økonomiske og administrative fag, maritime fag, samfunnsvitskap og humaniora, i tillegg til phd-utdanninger i datateknologi, ansvarlig innovasjon og regional utvikling og i nautiske operasjoner.

Fakultet har fem institutt med om lag 500 tilsette og 5700 studenter. Fakultetet blir ledet av dekan som har det overordnet ansvaret for den faglige og administrative virksomheten ved fakultetet og som rapporterer til rektor. Hoveddelen av fakultetet sin virksomhet er i Haugesund, Bergen, Sogndal og Førde, men fakultetet har også aktivitet ved campus Stord.


Institutt for maskin- og maritime studium har om lag 900 studentar og 80 tilsette i Bergen og Haugesund. Instituttet har ansvaret for fagtilbud innen maritime utdanninger, maskinfag, marinteknikk, bærekraftig produksjon og sirkulærøkonomi og energi- og havteknologi. Havrommet er en fellesnemnar - sammen med fagfelt som samhandling mellom mennesker, organisasjon og teknologi (inkludert system), framtidas utfordringer i blant annet grønn omstilling, og økt digitalisering og autonomi i maritim og marin sektor. Instituttet har syv bachelorprogram, to masterprogram og ph.d.-i Nautiske operasjoner. Det er flere mulige veier til gjennomgående utdanninger fra bachelor til ph.d. i instituttet.

Meitheal Mara, Cork’s community boatyard and maritime training centre, invites applications for the position of Festival & Events Manager for the annual Ocean to City – An Rás Mór and Cork Harbour Festival. The position is for the equivalent of 32 hours per week, with an annual salary of €34,212. Flexibility with be required in the annual distribution of hours, with a higher proportion worked during the periods leading up to events. The role is based at Meitheal Mara’s offices at Crosses Green House, Cork and is offered on a contract of indefinite duration, subject to continued funding. Cork Harbour Festival Cork Harbour Festival is the largest annual event in Cork Harbour offering a 10-day celebration of Ireland’s maritime culture. The festival features over 100 different events, organised by 50+ cultural, community, sporting and maritime event partners across Cork City and County. The festival is coordinated and promoted by Meitheal Mara, attracting approximately 30,000 visitors annually. Funded by Fáilte Ireland, Cork City Council, Cork County Council and the Port of Cork, the festival provides an important platform for Meitheal Mara’s wider work: celebrating Ireland’s maritime culture, connecting people with our waterways and creating opportunities to participate on the water. Ocean to City – An Rás Mór Ocean to City – An Rás Mór is the flagship event of Cork Harbour Festival and the largest event directly organised and delivered by Meitheal Mara. It is Ireland’s largest multi-craft rowing and paddling race, attracting 600+ participants annually – of which a third are international. The Festival & Events Manager will have overall responsibility for the planning and delivery of the Ocean to City race, from initial planning, stakeholder engagement and participant promotion through to event delivery, evaluation and reporting. The Festival & Events Manager The successful candidate will coordinate all aspects of Ocean to City –An Rás Mór, working closely with Meitheal Mara staff, volunteers, participants, partners, sponsors, suppliers, agencies, funders and other stakeholders to ensure the successful delivery of a safe, inclusive and well-managed event. The role also oversees Meitheal Mara’s coordination of Cork Harbour Festival, with overall responsibility for the successful delivery of the programme. The Festival Manager will support and line-manage the Marketing, PR & Programme Coordinator, who will focus on festival programming, event partner liaison, marketing and communications. The role will also coordinate and deliver Meitheal Mara’s Dragon Boat Challenge corporate fundraiser, held at regular times throughout the year. The successful candidate will have strong event management experience coupled with experience in managing and coordinating a mixed team of staff and volunteers in a community setting. For further details and a full job description please see: https://corkharbourfestival.com/recruiting-festival-events-manager/

jobs.title: Head of HR Operations & Employee Relations
jobs.description:
Head of HR Operations & Employee Relations

Join us in building a sustainable society powered by clean energy and reliable connections! As the current role holder is moving on to new challenges, we are looking for a business-oriented Head of HR Operations and Employee Relations to join our HR Leadership Team and help shape Enersenses employee experience through HR operations, services and employment matters.

In this role, you will play a key role in the continuous development of our HR operations, HR services provided to our personnel, payroll and employment-related matters main focus being in Finland. You will lead HR services, the development of HR processes, systems and digitalization, and the payroll team. You will be responsible for developing HR legal practices, guiding the organisation on employment-related matters, and ensuring compliance and continuous dialogue. You will lead a team of seven professionals. Your direct reports will include the Payroll Manager, HR Services Manager, and HR system, process and digitalization specialists.

The position is part of our international Group HR Leadership Team and reports to the EVP, HR, HSEQ, Communications and Sustainability. The preferred work location is our Pasila office in Helsinki, with flexible hybrid working opportunities.

Together with your expert team, you will drive a positive employee experience and smooth HR operations through the following key responsibilities:

Lead HR operations and services
* Lead and develop HRM and employment-related processes
* Drive the development of HR systems and digitalization of the processes
* Lead the HR services function and its continuous improvement

Develop the payroll function and salary payment systems and processes
* Lead the payroll operating model development (mainly external payroll)
* Develop related systems, with a focus on master data and time and attendance systems
* Ensure compliance with legal requirements, such as the EU Pay Transparency Directive
* Lead collaboration with our service providers

Lead HR legal and employment-related matters
* Ensure compliance with employment-related legislation and collective and local agreements
* Develop relations with personnel representatives by continuous dialogue and collaboration
* Develop guidelines and negotiate and implement changes related to employment-related matters
* Support the business and HR colleagues on a wide range of employment-related matters

What do we expect from you?
* A masters degree, preferably in law, and 6-8 years of relevant experience in a business environment. We also welcome candidates with a degree in another field who have extensive experience and expertise in employment matters
* Strong collaboration, communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills
* A forward-looking mindset to developing processes and ways of working in a fast-changing and growing international organisation
* Ability to combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution
* Fluency in English and Finnish.

Whats in it for you?Why join Enersense?
* A broad and influential director-level role where you will shape HR operations, services, systems, and employment practices across the organisation
* Genuine ownership of a business-critical HR agenda, with the opportunity to make a visible impact as a member of the Group HR Leadership Team
* The opportunity to lead and develop an experienced team of HR services, payroll, systems, process, and digitalization professionals
* Close collaboration with business leaders, HR colleagues, and external partners on complex and business-critical employment, payroll, and HR operations matters
* A meaningful opportunity to build efficient, compliant, and future-ready HR operations that support our people, our business, and Enersenses contribution to a more sustainable society
* As our company grows it offers you the opportunity to grow with us

Dont meet every requirement?

We know that some candidates apply only when they meet every qualification. If this opportunity excites you but your experience does not fully match all the requirements, we still encourage you to apply.

Are you up for the challenge? Apply for a role where you can develop your skills through meaningful and challenging work in a supportive community.

Please send your application as soon as possible, as we begin interviews during the application period and fill the position once the right candidate is found.

For more information about the position, please contact: Anu Henttonen +358 40 509 3169 Thu 8.10. and Tue 13.10 or by emailanu.henttonen@enersense.com

1\. The Storekeeper needs ensure that the EE Policies, Procedures and Processes are implemented, enforced and, when applicable, developed, and improved.

2\. Maintain day to day relations with the internal clients (HODs) on Supply Chain related topics.

3\. Review and monitor performance against inventory procedures and strategies to improve performance and effectiveness on the warehouse and inventory location for EE with direct communication to our office staff (Houston HQ)

- Inventory counts

- POs received on board vessels - Inbound Cargo Manifests (MRR)

- Reverse Logistics implementation (Outgoing cargo manifests (MTL) and Manifest for Exportation (MFE)

- New Equipment, Spares, or consumables requests preparation (NSCR) for office generation in the system.


5\. Perform Material Requisitions receptions in a timely manner.

6\. Assist the logistic and procurement dept. to follow up on the OS&D process (Overage, shortage, or Damage).

7\. Keep Chief Engineer fully updated on spare parts and consumable status.

8\. Control and order spare parts and consumables for all Departments (Replenishment Plan)

9\. Follow up, receiving, delivery of spare parts and stores, inspection & storing.

10\. Control, registration and updating data on regular basis in NSE Stock control program.

11\. Maintain current files for Open and Closed Requisitions, Purchase Order, Packing List and Invoices. Over, Short and Damaged OSD, Return to stock.

12\. Daily issues slip form monitoring and proper follow up.

13\. Adequate protection of all parts and tools in storerooms.

14\. Ensures that borrowed tools and instruments are properly returned in good condition and keep tracking report up to date.

15\. Control of and keep storerooms and adjacent compartments clean and tidy, well organized, and spare parts correctly labeled and safely stored.

16\. Maintains good housekeeping practices in all storage areas of the warehouse and outside storage areas

17\. Monitoring all Stores are taken to the Warehouse location in a timely manner after physical reception takes place on board and further distribution to the HOD (Heads of Department) is done of cargo reception.

18\. Maintains good housekeeping of equipment, receiving areas, and storage area following HSE protocols and procedures.

19\. Maintain Filing of Requisition forms, ensuring that they are properly filled up and acknowledged by the requesting parties.

20\. Enter data into a database or other computerized system to maintain up-to-date stock records

21\. Implement Cycle counts onto Warehouse shelving and racking structures (Including re organization and material placement inside the location)

22\. Relabeling of materials as required.

23\. Process Implementation for warehouse improvements.

24\. Weekly chemicals and lubes compressed gas bottles, medical supplies, medicines, and personal protective equipment inventory Count.

25\. Transfer orders generation for material transfers within EE Fleet Vessels.

26\. Handover notes preparation for storekeeper relief.

**Crew Matrix Requirements (STCW):**

- Maritime English – CEFR B1

- Cyber Security Awareness

- Bullying and Harassment

- STCW V/1.2.1 Basic training for LNG Tanker Cargo Ops

- STCW VI/1 Basic safety

- STCW VI/6.2 - Designated security duties


**Technical Competence:**

- Understanding of Warehousing and Inventory management procedures and processes.

- Good Knowledge in Supply chain information systems (ERP).

- Previous Warehousing and Inventory control experience strongly preferred, or ability to demonstrate comparable knowledge and skills. (Preferred 3 years).

- Strong team spirit and customer service orientation.

- Willing to work extended periods of time and perform physical activities


Previous experience on an FSRU vessels is required.

jobs.title: PhD position at the Department of Geography
jobs.description:
UiB - Knowledge that shapes society

UiB shall be among Europe's leading universities, internationally recognized for high quality in research and education. As a societal institution, we shall contribute to sustainable and democratic development and be an attractive and inclusive place to study and work.

Video: https://youtu.be/i4SDcLir6OcPhD position

There is a vacancy for a PhD position in System Dynamics at the Department of Geography. The position is within the project INTEGRATOR and for a fixed-term period of 3 years. Starting date is latest 1 April 2027.

System Dynamics Group at the Department of Geography

The System Dynamics group carries out research in several areas. The most important areas are: sustainability transitions, natural resources management, water-energy-food-ecosystems (WEFE) nexus, and model-based learning and communication. The group makes use of a variety of tools and techniques: stakeholder mapping, governance analysis, participatory modeling, non-linear feedback modeling, computer simulation, non-linear model analysis, interactive learning environments and decision-laboratory experiments.


About the project/work tasks:

Description of the INTEGRATOR project

The position is within the EU Horizon Europe project ‘Integrated Innovation Ecosystems for Transformative Nexus Governance towards Enhanced Water Resilience (INTEGRATOR)’. The overarching project objective is to strengthen Europe’s climate-resilient and fair water management by enabling anticipatory, evidence-based decision making at river basin scale under changing climatic and socio-economic conditions, directly supporting the implementation of the EU water strategy. Specific objectives of INTEGRATOR pertaining to this call include: (1) promoting system-wide transformation in water governance and management to strengthen resilience, preparedness, and fair allocation; (2) establishing site-specific, stakeholder-led strategies; (3) creating seasonal and long-term foresight by developing and coupling a suite of models, including data-driven, process-based, and system-dynamics approaches; (4) delivering a digital water intelligence system orchestrated by a prompt compiler translating human language into executable simulations.

INTEGRATOR is built on six case studies in Germany, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Spain and Türkiye with various socio-economic, sectoral development, land use, water quality and water quantity challenges. Among these case studies, two of them are particularly relevant to this call: (1) Ergene River Basin (Türkiye), a 17K km2 watershed and a major industrial and agricultural hub with 2M inhabitants, facing severe pressure on groundwater resources, water quality and allocation. (2) Jucar River Basin – Albufera system in Spain, a highly interconnected river-water-coastal continuum centered on the 210 km2 Albufera Natural Park with high ecological value, facing pressures from intensive irrigated agriculture, and urban and industrial development.

Responsibilities following the position:

The research fellow will use participatory system dynamics modelling and computer simulations to support INTEGRATOR in all work packages (abbreviated as WP), with a concentrated focus on two WPs: WP3 (Participatory Co-Design for Resilient and Equitable Water Solutions using a Decision Theatre Approach) is going to strengthen inclusive and transformational governance through structured participatory process in the INTEGRATOR’s Decision Theatres (DTs). More specifically, WP3 will deal with stakeholder mapping, problem co-definition, participatory scenario analysis and policy exploration embedded in INTEGRATOR’s Decision Theatres Approach (DTA). WP6 (Digital Water Intelligence System and the HydroFellow) is going to provide a Digital Water Intelligence System (DWIS) and a prompt compiler, integrating multisource information, including models and model generated data. More specifically, WP6 will work on integrated hydrological and system dynamics modeling, site-specific digital twin development and integration, and the prompt compiler HydroFellow development through interaction with the DTs. The research fellow will be working on the Ergene and Albufera case studies to fundamentally support the activities under WP3 and WP6 through systems thinking, dynamic systems modeling and computer simulations.


Qualifications and personal qualities:
  • The applicant must hold a master’s degree in System Dynamics or another discipline with a strong system, modeling and simulation focus. The master’s degree must have been completed by the application deadline.
  • The requirements are generally a grade B or better on the Master thesis and for the master’s degree in total.
  • Applicants must demonstrate a strong interest in socio-economic-hydrological scenario building; experience in participatory model-building is desirable.
  • Applicants must have strong quantitative and computational foundations.
  • Teaching assistance experience in the field of System Dynamics will be considered an advantage.
  • The applicant must be proficient in both written and oral English. Proficiency in Spanish and/or Turkish languages will be considered an advantage.
  • Applicants must be able to work independently and in a structured manner.
  • Applicants should have experience of working as a member of a multidisciplinary and multicultural research team and demonstrate good collaborative skills.
  • Experience in interdisciplinary working, linking social/economic and environmental sciences, is desirable.
  • Personal and relational qualities will be emphasized. Ambitions and potential will also count when evaluating the candidates.
  • The place of work for this position is Bergen, and the work requires that you are physically present at the Department of Geography on a daily basis.

Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an interview. 


About the PhD position:

The duration of the PhD position is 3 years. 

About the PhD training:

As a PhD research fellow, you will take part in the PhD programme at the Faculty of Social Sciences, UiB. The programme corresponds to a period of three years and leads to the PhD degree. To be eligible for admission you must normally have an educational background corresponding to a master’s degree with a scope of 120 ECTS credits, which builds on a bachelor’s degree with a scope of 180 ECTS credits (normally 2 + 3 years), or an integrated master’s degree with a scope of 300 ECTS credits (5 years). Master’s degrees must normally include an independent work of a minimum of 30 ECTS credits. It is expected that the topic of the master’s degree is connected to the academic field to which you are seeking admission.


We can offer:
  • Salary as PhD (code 1017) NOK 593 700,- per year. Automatic salary increases for up to 3 years with a 3% annual increase 
  • A good and professionally challenging working environment
  • Enrolment in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
  • Good welfare benefits

Project proposal:

A research proposal of maximum 2500 words (excluding reference list) must accompany the application. The project description should present the topic, the research questions(s) and choice of theory and methods. It should also include a progress plan for the different parts of the project. The research proposal must also include a short description of how the applicant envisions a fit with the INTEGRATOR project. Admittance to the PhD programme will be based on the research proposal. 


Your application must include:
  • A cover letter including a brief account of your research interests and motivation for applying for the position
  • The names and contact information for two reference persons. One of them must be the main advisor for the master's thesis or equivalent thesis
  • Project proposal
  • CV
  • Transcripts and diplomas showing completion of the bachelor's and master's degrees.
  • Relevant certificates/references
  • A list of academic publications
  • Academic publications that you want to submit for assessment (including your master’s thesis or equivalent)
  • If you have a master's degree from an institution outside of the Nordic countries, or a 2-year discipline- based master's degree (or the equivalent) in a subject area other than the one associated with the application, you may later in the application process be asked to submit an overview of the syllabus for the degree you have completed

The application and appendices with certified translations into English or a Scandinavian language must be uploaded at Jobbnorge following the link on this page marked “Apply for this job”.

Closing date: November 1, 2026.

Applications submitted without a project proposal or applications sent as e-mails will not be considered. Only submitted documents will be subjected to an expert assessment.


General information:

Detailed information about the position can be obtained by contacting Professor Ali K. Saysel, ali.saysel@uib.no.

Practical questions regarding the application procedures, please contact the HR section at: personal.svfa-sm@uib.no. 

Appointed research fellows will be admitted to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Social Sciences. Questions about the programme may be directed to Adviser Elina Troscenko, elina.troscenko@uib.no

Diversity is a strength that enables us to solve our tasks even better. UiB therefore needs qualified employees regardless of gender, ethnicity, religion, worldview, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, and age.

The University of Bergen applies the principle of public access to information when recruiting staff for academic positions.

Information about applicants may be made public even if the applicant has asked not to be named on the list of persons who have applied. The applicant must be notified if the request to be omitted is not met.

The successful applicant must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at all times.

We encourage applicants with disabilities, immigrant backgrounds, or gaps in their CV to apply. By indicating such circumstances in your application, you may receive favourable consideration. We ensure that at least one qualified applicant from each of these groups is invited for an interview as part of our commitment to inclusivity and equal opportunity. For further information about the recruitment process, click here.


Life as a PhD candidate at UiB

Marion Claireaux tells about life and work as a PhD candidate at UiB.

jobs.title: Researcher or Doctoral Researcher in justice and sustainability transitions
jobs.description:
How can we make the ongoing energy transition more just, and who gets to define what a just transition means? As societies pursue more sustainable energy and industrial systems, questions of justice are becoming increasingly central to public debate and decision-making. This position offers the opportunity to contribute to research addressing these questions in the context of Finlands emerging battery industry. This position requires excellent Finnish language skills and a strong command of English.

LUT University is looking for a researcher or doctoral (junior) researcher to join the Academy Research Fellowship project Circuits of Justice: Exploring Normative and Spatial Dimensions of Justice Across Finlands Battery Supply Chain. The four-year project, led by Dr Alicja Dankowska in LUT Universitys Energy and Society research group, examines how justice claims emerge, circulate, and evolve throughout the Finlands battery supply chain. Taking a whole-systems perspective, the project explores how stakeholders understand, negotiate, and contest different dimensions of justice across places, sectors, and scales.

What your work will be like

As a member of the project team, you will work closely with the principal investigator and contribute to all major stages of the research process. Your work will involve studying policy, media, and public debates on the development of Finlands battery industry through discourse analysis. You will also conduct multi-sited fieldwork, including interviews, focus groups, document analysis, and participant observation.

You will help desing and facilitate stakeholder co-creation workshops that explore pathways towards a more just transition and take part in analysing and interpreting research data with the project team. You will also contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations, and other dissemination activities and participate in international research collaboration, including research visits to Norway and Spain.

What we expect

We are looking for an independent, proactive, and collaborative researcher who enjoys working with colleagues, stakeholders, and international research partners.

Applicants for the researcher position must have a relevant doctoral degree and advanced research experience. Applicants for the doctoral (junior) researcher position must hold a relevant masters degree.

You should have a background in a relevant social science discipline, such as sociology, political science, human geography, anthropology, sustainability studies, environmental policy, or a related field. You also need to have experience in discourse analysis – particularly policy or media analysis – as well as strong qualitative research skills and interest in fieldwork.

Knowledge of energy transitions, sustainability transitions, science and technology studies (STS), or just transitions and energy justice is highly desirable. Experience related to batteries, critical raw materials, mining, energy systems, or industrial transitions is considered an advantage.

What we offer

This position offers an opportunity to contribute to a novel and societally relevant research project in close collaboration with national and international research partners. You will be able to develop your qualitative and interdisciplinary research expertise while receiving support for scientific publishing and conference participation. The project also provides opportunities for international research mobility and a collegial, supportive research environment within LUT Universitys Energy and Society research group.

We will fill the position at either of the following levels:

Doctoral (junior) researcher

- The position is full-time. It begins with a one-year term (including a six-month trial period) and may be extended by three years, depending on the progress of your studies and the quality of your research.

- The salary is set according to the Finnish university pay systems scale for teaching and research staff (requirement level 2). The starting salary is approximately EUR 3,100 per month, depending on experience and qualifications.

- The selected candidate must apply for the right to pursue doctoral studies at the LUT Doctoral School within the first two months of employment.

Researcher

- The employment relationship is part-time (70% of full-time) with a fixed term running until 31 August 2030 (including a six-month trial period).

- The salary is set according to the Finnish university pay systems scale for teaching and research staff (requirement levels 5–6). The starting salary is approximately EUR 4,300–5,000 per month, depending on qualifications and experience and based on the part-time workload.

The work starts as soon as possible, and the start date is negotiable. The position is based at LUTs Lappeenranta campus in Finland. LUT offers a hybrid work model that combines flexibility with regular on-campus presence. The position follows a system of 1,612 annual working hours under the collective agreement for Finnish universities. The hours are flexible and support work–life balance.



If you are eager to advance understanding of justice in sustainability transitions while developing your academic research career in an international environment, we encourage you to apply.



Interested? Please submit your application through the link below by 3 November 2026 at 23:59 (Finnish local time, UTC+2). Fill out the online form and attach the following documents in English and in PDF format:

- A motivation letter, including research experience, skills, and motivation related to the research focus of the project (max. 1 page)

- Your curriculum vitae (max. 2 pages)

- A list of publications

- A copy of your degree certificate and a transcript of your academic records proving your eligibility for the position; if the original documents are not in English, Finnish, or Swedish, official certified translations into English or Finnish are required

- A link to your thesis or doctoral dissertation

Please specify which position you are applying for. Submit your application well before the deadline to allow time for uploading all attachments. Also, make sure you submit only one application. Only applications submitted through the online recruitment system will be considered. We will review applications on a rolling basis, and the position will be filled

jobs.title: Early Childhood Education Teacher (recruitment from abroad, permanent position in public sector daycare))
jobs.description:
Hello, Early Childhood Education Teachers! Are you interested in working in a public daycare in Finland, known for its high-quality education system? We offer a permanent full-time position, competitive salary, great employee benefits, free Finnish language training, apartment, relocation support, and a clear pathway to living and working in Finland. Whether you are an experienced Early Childhood Education Teacher or newly qualified, we at the City of Helsinki would be delighted to hear from you!

In Finland, ECE teachers are highly trusted professionals. You have significant autonomy in planning pedagogical activities and are encouraged to use your professional expertise in everyday work. You support the holistic development of children aged 0-6 in an inclusive, child-centred environment. You work in a multi-professional team, sharing responsibility for childrens wellbeing and learning.

In Finland, ECE is part of the national education system and follows the Educare model, integrating care, education and teaching (read more from the Finnish National Agency for Education: https://www.oph.fi/en/education-system/early-childhood-education-and-care-finland). In practice, this means that:
Every moment is pedagogical
Play is the foundation of learning
Learning happens throughout the whole day
Nature and outdoor environments are used yearround
Childrens interests and questions guide learning

Your core responsibilities:
Plan, implement and assess play-based learning activities
Lead your groups pedagogical work together with childcare nurses
Observe and document childrens learning and development
Create and update individual learning plans in collaboration with families
Collaborate with colleagues and multidisciplinary professionals
Design inspiring learning environments indoors and outdoors

Our daycare units' opening hours range between 6:15-17:30, depending on families needs. As a full-time teacher you work 38.25 hours per week Monday-Friday.

We are looking for professionals who connect well with others and are open to learning and professional growth. You value teamwork and recognise that high-quality pedagogy is built together. You will enjoy this role if you want to fully use your pedagogical expertise and appreciate professional trust and autonomy. You are an advocate of play-based learning and see learning opportunities in everyday moments. As a professional you are reflective, curious and resilient.

Qualification and other requirements to start the Finnish language course in February 2027:
Right to work in Finland, for example, on the basis of EU/EEA citizenship
At least Bachelors degree in Early Childhood Education
At least level B2 in English language
Willingness and ability to commit to learning Finnish language prior to employment contract and relocation. The working language in our daycares is Finnish. During the language course we test your language skill development regularly.

Requirements to enter into a permanent employment contract in January 2028:
Reaching target level B1 in Finnish language
Decision from the Finnish National Agency of Education demonstrating eligibility to work as an ECE teacher in Finland
Criminal record extract from the Legal Register Centre
Proof that you do not have respiratory tuberculosis

We can only enter into a permanent employment contract with you if you meet all the above requirements.

We provide comprehensive support to make your relocation to Finland as smooth as possible:
Assistance with degree recognition process
Remote Finnish language training (10 months, part-time, 4x90min lessons every week + 4-8h/wk independent study, homework and assignments) which you can complete alongside your current employment
Pre-departure training also includes practical information about working and living in Finland
Support in registrations with Finnish authorities upon arrival (also for relocating family members)
Assistance in finding an apartment. As a City of Helsinki employee, you can rent a City-owned apartment and no rental deposit is required.

Language training and relocation schedule:
Feb'27-Dec'27: Finnish language training remotely. Attendance and active participation is essential.
Jan'28: Relocation to Finland and starting work.

Salary and benefits:
Starting salary: €3,298/mth +3-8% experience-based supplements for 5-10 yrs of relevant experience
ePassi benefit: €550/year (sports, culture, wellbeing, commuting)
Comprehensive private occupational health care
Paid annual leave: 23-28 days + 5 extra days for qualified teachers
Holiday bonus pay

Watch our teachers who have already relocated share their experiences of pedagogical work, life in Finland, and the support they received in the relocation process:

Melissa: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6eyjJjnxRiY
Yaiza: https://youtu.be/4IPA8d0pkI4

We warmly welcome you to join a workplace that values your expertise and recognises the potential in both you and the children!
